minimal_layout: MSTX NOW — the lag verdict headline with three tiles: MSTX price, lag vs last hour, monitor heartbeat (coloured when stale, not just timestamped). Non-firing states collapse from five sentences to two.
LEVEL — the CHEAP / FAIR / RICH word with three tiles: gap in MSTX terms, projected MSTX, BTC vs its 50-day. mNAV, target mNAV and BTC-per-share drop off the page.

ALERT LOG — the ledger cut to five columns (when, kind, lag MSTX, 60-min MSTX, 60-min vs BTC) with a narrow-screen variant, the scored tally underneath, and one corrected line stating the fire levels and the real gates (Rich ungated).

GAP CHART — the gap sub-chart alone, converted to MSTX terms so its dashed lines read -6% and +8% like everything else, with the last five closes labelled beneath it. The MSTR-vs-projection price chart goes.
WHAT IF — four boxes (BTC, MSTR, MSTX, STRC), three result cards (projected MSTX, gap, verdict), reset-to-live, and the edit-config-on-GitHub link. No slope toggle, no holdings inputs.

DETAILS (collapsed) — the four-row lag evidence table and the two regime read lines. Nothing else: cheap episodes, the regime table, the level lines, the slope sweep and the target-rule footer are cut.
summary: The MSTX tab shows 14 number cards, 2 charts, 4 tables, a 4-row threshold list and 6 input boxes across roughly 760 lines, and a large fraction of it is the same six numbers rendered again in a different box. The worst offender is WHAT IF: it seeds from the live quotes, so on every page load its six cards restate the four level cards directly above it. The lag threshold is printed three separate times within 60 lines (the headline sentence, the fires list, the tvLine paragraph), and the monitor strip at the top of SHORT-TERM LOG repeats three numbers that are all already on screen in larger type. In DETAILS, the same four cheap episodes and the same +5.9%/-4.3% regime split appear in an 11-column table, a 6-column table, a prose line and the price chart's green shading. Two defects matter more than the noise. First, the tab tells him Rich is muted unless BTC is below its 50-day; that gate was removed on 9/17, the config and the monitor both fire Rich in either regime, and the string rich_gate does not appear anywhere in index.html, so the one line documenting when he gets a ping is simply wrong. Second, mstr-model.json is as_of 2026-09-16 and today is 9/18, which trips the staleness gate and blanks the MSTX price card and the projected-MSTX subtitle, so one of the three things he uses this tab for is not on screen right now with no warning that the file needs regenerating. Two more are worth fixing while in there: a dead monitor renders the same OFF HOURS as a healthy sleeping one, and the alert ledger is the only table with no narrow-screen variant, so his phone has to scroll sideways for the most important table on the page. My cut: six sections, three tiles per verdict instead of four to six cards, one chart instead of two, one table instead of four.
